speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; you mentioned experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty. To understand what's happening, how long has it been since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the shooting pain when eating suggests referred otalgia, likely involving the auriculotemporal nerve. Given your history of chronic infections and recent surgery, we must rule out a cholesteatoma recurrence or granulation tissue. REQUEST TEST: High-resolution CT of the temporal bone. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the post-operative CT scan if available.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Ear-Teeth Syndrome)

The "normal" readings you provided do not explain the specific nature of your shooting pain triggered by eating and the tenderness when wearing earrings. Based on your history of tympanoplasty and the pattern of pain, this is highly suggestive of nerve entrapment or irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve. Do you notice any specific trigger points on your jaw or temple area when I press gently?
